item.title: Russia, US see grounds for financial ties, Russian finance minister says
item.description: Dialogue between Russia and the U.S. should continue to find common ground in economics, which should make it easier to discuss political issues, Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said, according to an Interfax news agency report on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dialogue between Russia and the U.S. should continue to find common ground in economics, which should make it easier to discuss political issues, Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov said, according to an Interfax news agency report on Wednesday. Asked about a bilateral [USN:L1N44S15H TEXT:"meeting"] with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent held on Monday at the G20 finance leaders conference in North Carolina, Siluanov said both countries have agreed that there are grounds for developing financial ties despite complications, Interfax reported. Siluanov, who said he was meeting with Bessent for the first time, said he believed that people from the financial world sometimes may find common understanding faster than politicians. "So we must always keep talking; we need to continue the dialogue. If we find strong points of common interest - and they do exist - we need to develop them. Then political issues will also be easier to resolve," he said, according to Interfax. Reuters reported on Monday that a source familiar with the ministers' meeting said Bessent made clear to Siluanov no economic relief for Russia or agreements on other issues were possible until its war in Ukraine ends.

item.title: Colin Kaepernick says NFL blackballing him: 'I watch college football'
item.description: A decade after his stance against racial injustice made headlines far beyond the sports world, former San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick says that while his mission goes on, his love for the NFL is long gone.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A decade after his stance against racial injustice made headlines far beyond the sports world, former San Francisco 49ers quarterback Colin Kaepernick says that while his mission goes on, his love for the NFL is long gone. Speaking with NBC News, the 38-year-old admitted he no longer watches the NFL, saying, "I'm not gonna support an organization that one, is actively blackballing me, but two, has targeted my brothers who have been protesting as part of this as well. I watch college football." During the 2016 preseason, Kaepernick and then-49ers teammate Eric Reid kneeled during the national anthem before a game. While he had previously sat on the bench during the anthem earlier that preseason, the image of him and Reid on a knee while their teammates stood for the anthem quickly circulated around the world. At the time, he told the NFL Network, "I am not going to stand up to show pride in a flag for a country that oppresses Black people and people of color. To me, this is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way. There are bodies in the street and people getting paid leave and getting away with murder." Kaepernick, who led the 49ers to the Super Bowl to conclude the 2012 season, was out of the league after 2016 and would never play again. He and Reid would later sue the NFL alleging collusion in keeping them out of the league. They settled in 2019. Kaepernick has since devoted his time to initiatives such as Know Your Rights camps, whose aim is "to advance the liberation and well-being of Black and Brown communities through education, self-empowerment, mass-mobilization and the creation of new systems that elevate the next generation of change leaders," and helping pay for independent autopsies for people who died as a result of incidents involving police. Asked by NBC if he thinks about his football legacy, Kaepernick said, "I don't think about legacy a whole lot. What I think about is what are the areas that I can do work that I think are going to have an impact and help us move towards that future together. At the end of the day, people will decide what that legacy is, and hopefully that's a positive one." Kaepernick wrote a memoir, "The Perilous Fight," that will be available on Sept. 15. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rockies beat Orioles, end franchise-record 10-game home losing streak
item.description: TJ Rumfield homered in the seventh inning to break a tie and the Colorado Rockies beat the Baltimore Orioles 4-2 in Denver on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: TJ Rumfield homered in the seventh inning to break a tie and the Colorado Rockies beat the Baltimore Orioles 4-2 in Denver on Tuesday night. Adael Amador also went deep and singled and Jake McCarthy and Brett Sullivan had two hits each for Colorado (53-86), which snapped a franchise-worst 10-game home losing streak. It was 2-2 in the seventh when Mickey Moniak reached on an error by second baseman Jackson Holliday. One out later, Rumfield homered off Luis De Leon (0-1) to give the Rockies the lead. It was his 14th of the season. Jaden Hill (1-3) pitched an inning of relief and Jordan Romano picked up his 14th save. Holliday homered among his three hits for Baltimore (69-70), whose four-game winning streak ended. The Orioles fell 1 1/2 games behind Cleveland for the final wild-card spot in the American League. Colorado initially went ahead with a two-out rally in the third inning against starter Kyle Bradish. Amador gave the Rockies a 1-0 lead with his second homer of the season, and Zac Veen nearly made it back-to-back home runs when he tripled off the top of the wall in right. McCarthy singled up the middle to drive in Veen. Bradish gave up two runs on six hits in five innings. Baltimore got a run back in the fourth inning. Carlos Narvaez led off with a single and went to third on Pete Alonso's one-out hit. Gunnar Henderson hit a sharp grounder to first that Rumfield snared and touched the bag for the out before getting Alonso in a rundown to end the inning. Narvaez scored before Alonso was tagged out. The Orioles threatened in the fifth when they loaded the bases with two outs to chase starter Gabriel Hughes. Brennan Bernardino came on to retire Henderson on a popout. Hughes allowed one run on four hits in 4 2/3 innings. Holliday evened things in the seventh with a two-out solo homer to right, his seventh of the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Banks rush to swap higher-risk credit assets for BoE cash
item.description: British banks are increasingly pledging higher-risk assets such as loans linked to high-interest store cards and vehicle leases as collateral at the Bank of England, a Reuters review of BoE filings shows.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Rovnick, Lawrence White, David Milliken
item.content:encoded: British banks are increasingly pledging higher-risk assets such as loans linked to high-interest store cards and vehicle leases as collateral at the Bank of England, a Reuters review of BoE filings shows. On August 18, banks pledged £1.9 billion worth of the BoE's highest-risk type of collateral at its weekly auction for six-month funds, its data shows, the most since March 2020 and three times as much as in the previous week. In total, Reuters calculations show the BoE has about £17.8 billion of what it calls "Level C" collateral on its books from its Indexed Long-Term Repo (ILTR), up from £8.7 billion a year ago and under £1 billion in mid-2024. Such transactions show the extent to which Britain's central bank is exposed to higher-risk and potentially illiquid assets. The European Central Bank, meanwhile, has tightened its criteria for acceptable collateral in recent years, worried that a central bank stamp of approval increases demand for riskier securities that could be hard to sell in a crisis. A BoE spokesperson said the ILTR was designed to allow firms to use a broad range of assets as collateral while allowing the BoE to protect itself through what it described as robust risk management. INTENDED CONSEQUENCE British commercial banks use cash held in accounts at the BoE for wholesale transactions. The growing use of the ILTR to receive this cash is an intended consequence of the BoE's 2022 decision to [USN:L8N3U40TK TEXT:"reverse"] the £895 billion of quantitative easing it undertook from 2009 to 2021, which flooded the financial system with cash. Reuters analysis of the BoE's Level C collateral list showed that the British central bank accepts a range of products in categories that the ECB has disallowed under its tighter rules on acceptable loan security, including several debt products that package up and sell the future payments on homeowners' mortgages. The securitisation of mortgage-backed debt and other loans was a major contributor to the 2008 financial crisis as it encouraged risk-taking by lenders who were able to quickly sell the debt on. "The BoE has got good reasons for wanting to buy grade C assets but there’s a risk that if they do too much then that can encourage bad lending. I think they probably understand that already," said William Allen, a visiting fellow at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research and a former head of the BoE's money markets division. The central bank's spokesperson said the BoE continually reviews its framework to ensure that it remains consistent with its risk tolerance objectives. The BoE charges banks a higher interest rate and applies a bigger "haircut" to riskier assets, meaning it lends less than the asset's full value to protect itself from losses. Level C collateral has made up between a fifth and a quarter of the collateral accepted at the ILTR over the past year, but growing use of the facility means that in absolute terms it has more than doubled. "It is possible that the non-BoE market for these assets might not be as active as it was because there's a lower appetite for credit in private markets," said Moyeen Islam, fixed income analyst at Barclays. The $3.5 trillion global private credit industry has expanded rapidly in recent years with promises of higher yields, but also drawn [USN:L4N40R0UW TEXT:"growing scrutiny"] from regulators amid a slew of negative headlines and high-profile losses. HOME LOANS, VEHICLE LEASES, STORE CARDS Investec-linked Temese Funding's loan notes, which S&P Global says are backed by heavy equipment and vehicle leases that feature large late-stage instalments known as balloon payments, are on the BoE's list of Level C collateral. The ECB in effect excluded such products from its acceptable collateral pool in January, analysis of the rule change by law firm Jones Day showed. The BoE does not detail which specific assets on its Level C list have been used as collateral in the ILTR. Securities issued by Harben Finance, which public filings show is controlled by Barclays and owns payments on buy-to-let mortgages that were originated by former UK lender Bradford & Bingley before its 2008 government rescue, are also on the BoE's Level C list. Some tranches of the debt have been downgraded twice by Fitch Ratings and once by S&P Global in the past year. Among other assets eligible for the BoE's auction are loan notes backed by KKR-backed NewDay's credit cards, which Fitch Ratings said were aimed at higher-risk borrowers, and debt issued in 2024 by the Small Business Origination Loan Trust, which parcels up and sells loan payments from company owners who have borrowed through Funding Circle's financing platform. S&P Global said in an August 21 note that almost a fifth of the loans in this pool of Funding Circle debt would likely default. A spokesperson for Funding Circle declined to comment.

item.title: India's ICICI Bank mobilises $17.9 billion under RBI foreign currency deposit scheme
item.description: ICICI Bank has mobilised about $17.88 billion under the Reserve Bank of India's foreign currency non-resident deposits scheme through August 31, the private lender said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ICICI Bank (ICBK.NS) has mobilised about $17.88 billion under the Reserve Bank of India's foreign currency non-resident deposits scheme through August 31, the private lender said on Wednesday. Here are some key details: The bank said loans provided by international branches and subsidiaries against such deposits stood at $9 billion The lender has also issued $3.63 billion in guarantees to other banks for loans backed by the deposits In June, the Reserve Bank of India [USN:L4N42G1HH TEXT:"introduced"] a set of foreign exchange measures, including concessional swap facilities aimed at boosting overseas borrowing by state-run firms and attracting foreign currency non-resident deposits The RBI's foreign exchange forward position [USN:L4N44S152 TEXT:"climbed"] to an all-time high of $136.7 billion in July, fueled by a surge in overseas deposits following the central bank's measures to attract dollar inflows and support the rupee

item.title: Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) closer to return than 'some think'
item.description: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty might be back in the lineup for the season opener against the Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas general manager John Spytek said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty might be back in the lineup for the season opener against the Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas general manager John Spytek said. Jeanty did not participate in Tuesday's practice as he recovers from an ankle injury. Spytek said he could be back on the field sooner than expected. "I expect him to be back as quick as he can, maybe quicker than some people would expect," Spytek said Tuesday. Jeanty suffered the injury during an indoor practice on Aug. 23. Jeanty stayed down for a period and observers initially feared a more serious injury. If he's not cleared, Jeanty would likely be replaced by Mike Washington Jr. against the Dolphins. Washington had 23 carries for 168 yards in the preseason. Jeanty, 22, rushed for 975 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie last season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bangladesh offers rooftop solar incentives to ease power shortages
item.description: Bangladesh has launched an incentive programme for rooftop solar systems with battery storage, aiming to ease power shortages and reduce the country's dependence on imported fuels.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bangladesh has launched an incentive programme for rooftop solar systems with battery storage, aiming to ease power shortages and reduce the country's dependence on imported fuels. The South Asian nation of 175 million people is grappling with its worst power shortages in years, exacerbated by a lack of natural gas and concerns over global fuel supplies as the Iran war stokes broader Middle East tensions. Under the programme, consumers installing eligible rooftop solar systems by February 28, 2027 will receive 10.50 taka ($0.086) per kilowatt-hour for surplus electricity fed into the national grid for three years, according to a government notification. Bangladesh aims to generate 20% of its electricity, or about 5,500 megawatts, from renewable sources by 2030, with the share rising to 30% by 2040, as it seeks to cut reliance on imported fossil fuels. The announcement comes after power shortages climbed to nearly 4,000 megawatts at their peak in August, triggering widespread outages across the country. A shortage of natural gas has left power plants operating below capacity, while constraints on coal and fuel oil supplies have added to pressure on the electricity system. The government has been scrambling to secure oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) [USN:FWN4080DW TEXT:"supplies"], but long queues at compressed natural gas (CNG) stations, reduced industrial output and prolonged power cuts have highlighted the [USN:L4N3ZY0EO TEXT:"economic and social toll"] of the crisis. The government has capped the generation cost of rooftop solar power, including battery storage, at 8 taka per unit. The incentive payment includes a 20% profit margin and an additional premium. Consumers who install systems below the benchmark cost will be allowed to retain the savings. Bangladesh currently has about 1,559 megawatts of renewable energy capacity, most of it solar. Energy officials see rooftop systems as a faster way to expand electricity generation alongside utility-scale renewable projects. The instability in the Middle East has heightened concerns about fuel-price volatility and potential supply disruptions, underlining Bangladesh's vulnerability as a major energy importer. Authorities view rooftop solar as a relatively quick and cost-effective way to boost renewable energy capacity without requiring large tracts of land in one of the world's most densely populated countries. Battery storage is expected to help consumers use solar power beyond daylight hours and reduce demand on the grid during peak periods.

item.title: Sean Burke's effective start helps White Sox level series vs. Astros
item.description: Sean Burke threw 5 2/3 shutout innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox defeated the Houston Astros 5-1 on Tuesday, leaving each team with one win to begin a four-game series between division leaders.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Sean Burke threw 5 2/3 shutout innings as the visiting Chicago White Sox defeated the Houston Astros 5-1 on Tuesday, leaving each team with one win to begin a four-game series between division leaders. Colson Montgomery produced his second multi-hit game in as many nights for the White Sox (73-65), who maintained their three-game lead over the Guardians (70-68) in the American League Central. Cleveland topped the Toronto Blue Jays 6-1 earlier on Tuesday. The Astros (70-69) have dropped seven of their past 10 home games. Houston's lead in the AL West shrunk to one game over the Texas Rangers (69-70), who topped the Athletics 8-5 on Tuesday. Burke (8-6) recorded his fifth scoreless outing of the season, permitting just one hit and four walks. He struck out six. The right-hander overcame an inauspicious start, as he issued consecutive walks to Jeremy Pena and Yordan Alvarez to open the bottom of the first inning. Burke recovered quickly, retiring the ensuing three batters, including an inning-ending strikeout of LaMonte Wade Jr. Taylor Trammell blistered a one-out double to left-center field in the fifth inning for Houston's first hit. Burke responded by inducing a groundout from Cam Smith before striking out Pena to strand Trammell at third base. Burke capped his outing with a strikeout of Jose Altuve in the sixth. Astros right-hander Ronel Blanco, recalled from Triple-A Sugar Land to make his first major league appearance since Aug. 15, labored but still tossed four shutout innings. He allowed three hits and three walks while fanning three. Blanco stranded three baserunners in scoring position. The White Sox broke through against Astros reliever Kai-Wei Teng (5-7) for three runs in the fifth. With one out, Teng hit Sam Antonacci with a pitch before striking out Munetaka Murakami. Miguel Vargas walked, and Andrew Benintendi delivered an RBI single that snapped a scoreless tie. Montgomery followed with a two-run double to right that upped the lead to 3-0. Murakami and Montgomery walked in the seventh before Randal Grichuk delivered a two-run double off Astros reliever Tatsuya Imai for a 5-0 lead. Houston's Isaac Paredes hit a solo homer to left off Jordan Hicks in the eighth inning, his 18th long ball of the year. Montgomery finished 2-for-4 with a walk. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brewers rally from early deficit to beat Cubs
item.description: Christian Yelich and Joey Ortiz each hit two-run homers as the visiting Milwaukee Brewers evened their four-game series against the Chicago Cubs with a 9-4 win on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Christian Yelich and Joey Ortiz each hit two-run homers as the visiting Milwaukee Brewers evened their four-game series against the Chicago Cubs with a 9-4 win on Tuesday. Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang, William Contreras and Ortiz each had two hits for Milwaukee (86-53), which bounced back from a 17-3 loss in the series opener on Monday. The Brewers outhit Chicago 13-6 and moved eight games ahead of the second-place Cubs (78-61) in the National League Central. Trailing 3-0 after four innings, the Brewers scored nine runs over the next four frames to snap a two-game losing skid. Antonio Senzatela (10-4), one of five Milwaukee relievers, earned the victory. Chicago broke a scoreless tie with three runs against Robert Gasser in the fourth inning. Seiya Suzuki drew a leadoff walk, Alex Bregman hit an infield single, and Tyrone Taylor followed with a two-run double against his former team. Taylor then scored when Gasser mishandled the toss from first baseman Andrew Vaughn on Nico Hoerner's infield liner. Gasser gave up three runs (two earned) over 4 1/3 innings. Milwaukee got on the board in the fifth against Matthew Boyd when Luis Lara and Ortiz each singled with two outs before Lara scored on Cooper Pratt's single to left field. The Brewers pulled ahead with four runs on four hits in the sixth. After Daniel Palencia (2-2) replaced Boyd with one out and runners at second and third, Turang scored on a balk. Vaughn then tied the game with an RBI double, and Yelich put Milwaukee ahead 5-3 with a two-run homer to right-center field. Boyd allowed three runs on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings. He walked one and struck out three. Chicago pushed a run across with two outs in the bottom of the sixth when Hoerner scored from third on Carson Kelly's fielder's choice. BJ Murray Jr., making his debut, followed with a single for his first major league hit before Matt Shaw grounded out. Contreras doubled in a run with two outs in the seventh against Ryan Zeferjahn, who was replaced by Caleb Thielbar. After Jake Bauers walked, Sal Frelick delivered an RBI single to left. Bauers was thrown out at third on the play. Ortiz extended the Brewers' lead with a two-run homer against Tyler Ferguson with one out in the eighth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Honda tells suppliers to cut costs in $9 billion push to fend off China, documents show
item.description: Japan's Honda aims to cut more than $9 billion in costs over the next four years and has instructed suppliers to drastically reduce their prices, according to internal documents and one person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Maki Shiraki
item.content:encoded: Japan's Honda (7267.T) aims to cut more than $9 billion in costs over the next four years and has instructed suppliers to drastically reduce their prices, according to internal documents and one person familiar with the matter. The plan, reported here for the first time, is one of the most striking examples yet of how Japanese automakers are scrambling to deal with intensifying competition from China. BYD (002594.SZ) and other Chinese electric vehicle (EV) makers are capturing sizeable market share in Southeast Asia, Latin America and Europe, powered by advanced software and battery technology — and prices that are by far the industry's lowest. Honda, the world's largest motorcycle manufacturer, is trying to fix its struggling car business. It expects EV-related losses to ultimately total more than $12 billion, one of the biggest hits among global automakers, and is now shifting its focus to gasoline-electric hybrids. In May it reported its first-ever annual loss as a publicly traded company. The maker of the CR-V sport-utility vehicle now aims to save 1.5 trillion yen ($9.4 billion) by 2030, according to the documents and the person. This story is based on a Reuters review of internal company documents and interviews with two people familiar with the matter, both of whom declined to be identified because the information is not public. In a written response to questions, a Honda spokesperson declined to comment on specific cost-reduction targets or details of discussions with suppliers. The automaker was working with suppliers globally to improve competitiveness and reduce costs, including through the use of standardised parts, the spokesperson said. SPRING MEETING In spring of this year, Honda managers met with major suppliers at a convention centre in Utsunomiya, a city north of Tokyo near the automaker's R&D facility, according to the documents and the people. It was not clear how many suppliers attended. Honda managers briefed suppliers on the plan and said it would also look to source more components from Chinese suppliers, one of the people said. Each supplier was later presented with company-specific targets to cut costs, the people said. Honda is aiming to reduce costs by 30% in three key parts categories: pressed and forged components, electrical parts and parts related to software-defined vehicles (SDVs), according to the documents. Such a reduction would allow Japanese suppliers to better compete with Chinese rivals, the documents said. Honda's direct suppliers, or "tier-one" suppliers, were also asked to review how they procured materials and were urged to make use of standardised parts sourced from second- and third-tier suppliers, to help keep costs down, the documents showed. Honda managers also asked suppliers to expand their own use of Chinese-made components where possible, according to the documents. The cost-reduction targets were "extremely large" and it was not immediately clear whether they would be achievable, one of the sources said. The other person said that up until the spring meeting, Honda had not given the impression that it needed aggressive cost cuts. Now, the situation appeared to leave "no room for delay," the person added. On Monday, Honda and Nissan (7201.T) said they would [USN:L4N44S0L3 TEXT:"jointly develop"] standardised electronic control units for SDVs and aim to roll out an architecture built around them from the 2029 financial year. Honda CEO Toshihiro Mibe [USN:L1N42Y039 TEXT:"won support"] for his reappointment to the company's board in June. He has [USN:L6N42H0A2 TEXT:"faced pressure"] from former executives to step down over the company's performance. Last year, Honda and Nissan ended merger talks that would have created one of the world's largest automakers. In addition to Chinese competition, Honda and other automakers are [USN:L4N44P0I6 TEXT:"being squeezed"] by U.S. President Donald Trump's import tariffs and higher labour expenses. They also face the growing need to invest in research and development of technology as cars become more advanced, raising costs across the industry.

item.title: Shipping traffic via Strait of Hormuz stays below 10-day average, data shows
item.description: Four commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from 10 a day earlier and below the 10-day average of around 13, preliminary shipping data showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Four commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from 10 a day earlier and below the 10-day average of around 13, preliminary shipping data showed on Wednesday. The four vessels that transited were one very large crude carrier, one Panamax tanker, one Kamsarmax carrier and one intermediate tanker, initial data from shiptracker Kpler showed at 0200 GMT. Of the four vessels, one was entering the strait and three were leaving. The figures could change as some ships typically switch off transponders during the voyage. The United States said it had [USN:L8N44T0TP TEXT:"launched"] a series of air strikes against Iran on Tuesday, prompting Iranian retaliation, in the most serious escalation of the conflict between the two countries in weeks. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement the U.S. attacks would "tighten the lock" on the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway that carried about one-fifth of global oil consumption before the conflict. Meanwhile, 18 commodity vessels transited through the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Tuesday, another major maritime chokepoint in the Middle East, with seven vessels entering and 11 exiting. This compares with an average of around 24 ships going through Bab el-Mandeb over the past 10 days. Among the vessels travelling through the strait were two Aframax tankers and one Suezmax tanker.

item.title: Bond selloff deepens as inflation, oil prices jolt markets
item.description: Global bonds sold off sharply on Wednesday, extending a rout that is raising borrowing costs to multi-decade highs as the Middle East conflict pushes up energy prices, playing into investor fears about inflation and ballooning government debt.
item.dc:creator: Ankur Banerjee
item.content:encoded: Global bonds sold off sharply on Wednesday, [USN:L1N44T09D TEXT:"extending"] a rout that is raising borrowing costs to multi-decade highs as the Middle East conflict pushes up energy prices, playing into investor fears about inflation and ballooning government debt. Sovereign yields are a reference point for asset prices across financial markets and the higher price of money means higher mortgage rates for consumers and tough choices for government spending as funding costs climb. The yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury notes rose to a near three-year high of 4.81%, and a further climb toward 5% is likely to unsettle already jittery stock markets. Japan's 10-year yield was perched above 3%, a 30-year high. Australia's 10-year government bond yields rose to 5.198%, their highest level in over 15 years. Germany's bund futures slipped 0.45% to their lowest since 2011, while French OAT futures fell 0.5% to a record low. Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, said bond investors are increasingly demanding a higher premium for inflation, fiscal risks and the sheer amount of debt coming to market. "That means the selloff can overshoot, with 5% on the U.S. 10-year looking increasingly plausible before yields become sufficiently attractive to bring buyers back," Chanana said. A spree of bond sales from big tech companies aggressively raising money to fund the AI boom has added pressure on the sovereign bond market. Naka Matsuzawa, chief macro strategist at Nomura Securities in Tokyo, said hyperscalers' willingness to pay reasonably high rates was pulling up yields across the board, with the focus now on whether growth can rise along with them. "The (AI-driven) productivity leap needs to translate into higher wages," he said. If that materialises, he said, then the economy can live with higher rates. FISCAL FOCUS Investor focus has also been on what the Federal Reserve may do to contend with inflation that has remained above the central bank's 2% target with hawkish comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh last week leading traders to ramp up rate hike bets. Energy cost pressures continue to dog policymakers. Brent crude futures rose 1% to $95.61 per barrel on Wednesday, after gaining nearly 6% in the previous session. The 2-year U.S. Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, rose to 4.41%, its highest level since January 2025. Traders have priced in a rate hike in Europe next week and about a 68% chance of a U.S. rate hike the week after that. The scale of the structural shift in markets is highlighted by the rise in [USN:L1N44T043 TEXT:"Japanese"] government bond yields, once the lowest in the world, to lift the 10-year rate above 3% for the first time in 30 years on Tuesday. It was last at 3.01% on Wednesday morning hours. "Rising JGB yields not only reflect investor concerns over Japan’s fiscal outlook, with ambitious spending plans signalled for the coming years, but also global pressure on long-term funding costs," said Fred Neumann, Chief Asia economist at HSBC. The rising yields has put the spotlight on Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and her aggressive investment plan, along with Britain, France and Germany where big-spending governments are being given a reality-check by their creditors. "Japan and the UK look closest to the front line because rising yields are colliding with fiscal pressures and changing monetary regimes, while France also remains vulnerable given its debt trajectory," said Saxo's Chanana. British yields hit their highest since 2008 on Tuesday.

item.title: Pirates outlast Giants after blowing six-run lead
item.description: Brandon Lowe raced home from third base on a throwing error by substitute third baseman Osleivis Basabe with two outs in the bottom of the ninth inning, allowing the Pittsburgh Pirates, after blowing a six-run lead, to outlast the visiting San Francisco Giants 13-12 on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brandon Lowe raced home from third base on a throwing error by substitute third baseman Osleivis Basabe with two outs in the bottom of the ninth inning, allowing the Pittsburgh Pirates, after blowing a six-run lead, to outlast the visiting San Francisco Giants 13-12 on Tuesday night. Lowe led off the ninth against the fifth Giants pitcher, Carson Seymour (0-1), with his fourth hit of the game, a single, then advanced a base at a time on a Nick Gonzales single and an Oneil Cruz infield out. Seymour, who dropped a throw at first base that could have completed an inning-ending double play on Cruz's grounder, then got Rafael Flores Jr. to ground to third. Basabe, who had moved over from second base an inning earlier, made a nice stop, but then threw low to first, a ball Rafael Devers was not able to catch, ending the marathon game. Mason Montgomery (6-3), who pitched a scoreless top of the ninth, was credited with the win. Up 5-2 in the second inning and down 11-5 in the fifth, the Giants set up their late downfall with a five-run eighth. Drew Cavanaugh had a two-run double and Nate Furman had a game-tying, two-run single in the rally. The expected pitchers' duel between three-time All-Stars Logan Webb of the Giants and Paul Skenes of the Pirates never materialized. After the Pirates (68-71) had scored twice in the first, the Giants (57-82) got the merry-go-round in high gear with a five-run second that featured a three-run homer by Devers, his 31st of the season. The Pirates responded with a nine-run third, featuring five singles and two walks by the first seven batters Webb faced in the inning. When Spencer Horwitz and Lowe greeted Braxton Roxby with back-to-back hits, the Pirates had gone one complete turn of the lineup without recording an out, collecting seven singles and two walks. When Cruz, who had driven in the inning's first run with a single, plated a pair with a second single, the Pirates led 11-5. Webb was charged with nine runs on nine hits in two-plus innings. He walked two and struck out one. Skenes settled down after the five-run second, shutting out the Giants and retaining the 11-5 lead until getting pulled with two on and two out in the fifth. He handed the ball to Yohan Ramirez, who got Shay Whitcomb to pop up to end the inning. One out away from being eligible for his first win since July 19, Skenes allowed five runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings. He walked three and struck out four, throwing 95 pitches. Cruz joined teammate Lowe with a four-hit night and had a career-high-tying four RBIs for the Pirates, who won their third in a row. Horwitz, Gonzales and Jacob Gonzalez chipped in with two hits apiece. Turner Hill had four hits, Cavanaugh three, and Jonah Cox and Christian Koss two apiece for the Giants, who were attempting to win a third game in three days at three different locations. --Field Level Media

item.title: RBI's bid to lift Indian rupee put to test by oil, US yields
item.description: The Indian rupee is on course to open lower on Wednesday, pressured by a surge in oil prices and rising U.S. Treasury yields, threatening to blunt the momentum the currency has built with the central bank's intervention.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee is on course to open lower on Wednesday, pressured by a surge in oil prices and rising U.S. Treasury yields, threatening to blunt the momentum the currency has built with the central bank's intervention. The rupee is expected to open in the 95.02-95.06 range, according to traders, after settling at 94.95 to the dollar on Tuesday. The currency is on a three-day winning streak after touching a two-month high of 94.80 on Tuesday. The rupee's rally has come despite multiple headwinds and has been driven largely by aggressive intervention from the Reserve Bank of India, with flow-related dollar selling by foreign banks providing additional support, traders said. In recent sessions, the rupee has been among the better-performing Asian currencies. The question now is whether the RBI will step in again and absorb the pressure coming from higher oil prices, a currency trader at a bank said. At the moment, the central bank is effectively the only meaningful dollar seller in the market, and without its presence, it is difficult to see the rupee holding on to current levels, he added. The RBI's intervention comes against the backdrop of a surge in deposits from non-resident Indians, which has strengthened its firepower. Inflows under the FCNR(B) scheme topped $100 billion by the Aug. 31 deadline for banks to raise deposits eligible for concessional swaps with the RBI, the Financial Express reported. OIL, US YIELDS PRESSURE BUILDS Oil extended its rally in Asian trading, with Brent futures climbing to $95.50 a barrel after fresh exchanges of strikes between the U.S. and Iran overnight heightened fears of supply disruptions and dashed hopes of a near-term easing in Middle East tensions. The spike in crude prices reverberated through bond markets, pushing U.S. Treasury yields to their highest levels since late 2023.

item.title: US, Australia commit $580 million in support for Pacific Islands
item.description: The United States and Australia on Wednesday announced a combined $580 million in funding for the Pacific Islands, as both nations battle China for influence in the region.
item.dc:creator: Alasdair Pal, Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The United States and Australia on Wednesday announced a combined $580 million in funding for the Pacific Islands, as both nations battle China for influence in the region. Australia will offer a A$600 million ($430 million) package to combat drug smuggling in the region at a meeting of the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, including funds for enhanced aerial surveillance and more training for police and border officials. "The Pacific is our home and our family. That’s why it’s in Australia’s interests to work with our Pacific partners to combat organised crime," Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in a statement. "For the good of every country in the region, including our own – we need to work together to stamp out the illicit drug trade." In a separate announcement, the U.S. State Department said it will provide $150 million in funding to the region, including $60 million to help Pacific Islands countries address the global energy crisis by expanding fuel storage capacity and supporting grid stability. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau announced the funding at the forum that has so far been dominated by a [USN:L1N44T01G TEXT:"spat over Taiwan's participation"]. China, a major donor to the Pacific that views Taiwan as its own territory, has objected to the democratically run island's presence at the annual meeting of the 18-member forum. Members Australia and New Zealand said on Tuesday the bloc would decide the guest list. Palau, which is hosting this year's meeting, is among three Pacific nations that have maintained diplomatic ties with Taiwan. The meeting, which began on August 30, will run to September 4. ($1 = 1.4002 Australian dollars)

item.title: 10-run inning sparks Twins to second straight rout of Tigers
item.description: Royce Lewis went 3-for-4 and belted a three-run homer in a 10-run sixth inning as the Minnesota Twins smashed the Detroit Tigers 15-2 on Tuesday in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Royce Lewis went 3-for-4 and belted a three-run homer in a 10-run sixth inning as the Minnesota Twins smashed the Detroit Tigers 15-2 on Tuesday in Minneapolis. The Twins have outscored the Tigers 26-3 in the first two games of the three-game series, with Kody Clemens and Ryan Jeffers homering in each contest. Jeffers has three long balls in the series. Minnesota (67-72), riding a three-game winning streak, remains 3 1/2 games back of the Cleveland Guardians (70-68) for the third American League wild-card position. The Tigers (63-75) have lost seven straight road games and three games in a row overall. Andrew Morris opened for the Twins, giving up two hits and a run in his one inning, with no walks or strikeouts. Connor Prielipp (4-7) permitted three hits in five scoreless innings as the bulk reliever. The southpaw walked one and struck out five in a 73-pitch outing. Tigers starter Troy Melton (7-4) allowed six hits and seven runs, five earned, in 5 1/3 innings. The right-hander struck out four and walked one in 96 pitches. With the game tied 1-1, the Twins broke through in the fifth with three runs. Trevor Larnach led off with a walk, and Lewis doubled over Riley Greene's head in left. Walker Jenkins hit a one-out grounder right to shortstop John Peck, who threw home to get Larnach in a rundown. Catcher Dillon Dingler, however, tossed the ball into left field, allowing Larnach and Lewis to score to make it 3-1. The next batter, Luke Keaschall, gave the Twins a three-run lead with a double down the left field line to score Jenkins. Minnesota sent 15 batters to the plate while chasing Melton in the sixth inning. Josh Bell started it with a one-out single and Larnach was hit by a pitch. That set the table for Lewis, who delivered a three-run bomb to center to give the Twins a 7-1 lead. Kaelen Culpepper greeted reliever Kyle Finnegan with a double, and Jenkins walked. Keaschall made it six straight Twins to reach base, as his single drove in Culpepper. A sacrifice fly by Brooks Lee brought in Jenkins to give the Twins an eight-run lead. Jeffers' three-run homer to left boosted the margin to 12-1. Culpepper added a two-run single later in the inning. --Field Level Media

item.title: South Korean finance minister nominee vows to advance AI projects
item.description: South Korea's finance minister nominee vowed on Wednesday to quickly proceed with "mega projects" for AI investments and actively utilise policy capacity from a global chip boom.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's finance minister nominee vowed on Wednesday to quickly proceed with "mega projects" for AI investments and actively utilise policy capacity from a global chip boom. The pledge follows the government's unveiling on Tuesday of its most aggressive fiscal spending [USN:L1N44T02G TEXT:"plan"] on record for next year, which includes creating a fund for long-term investments, to strengthen the country's technological edge amid the global AI race. "(The government) will swiftly advance three mega projects to generate large-scale investments and growth power," Lee Hyoung-il said in a meeting with reporters. "(The government) will boldly support vulnerable sectors based on policy capacity secured from a semiconductor boom so that young people, small businesses and small- and medium-sized companies are not left out from growth," Lee said. Lee, who was [USN:L1N44R00D TEXT:"named"] as the country's new finance minister on Sunday, also vowed to expand pre-emptive investments in advanced technologies. The government expects tax revenue to increase 40.7% next year, with corporate tax receipts more than doubling as chipmakers earn record profits.

item.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. hints he may sit without new deal
item.description: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. hinted at the possibility of sitting out regular-season games without a new contract.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. hinted at the possibility of sitting out regular-season games without a new contract. Porter Jr. is entering the final year of his contract but practiced Tuesday for the first time since being activated from the physically unable to perform list on Sunday. A back injury limited him during preseason after he tweaked his back on the first day of training camp. Head coach Mike McCarthy said last week the two sides reached "an impasse" in contract talks, implying there would be no further discussions toward a long-term extension. But with Porter Jr. back on the field, he was asked if he would play in the regular season without an extension. "I don't know. I got to talk to the guys upstairs and my agents about that," he said. McCarthy said the Steelers are not certain if Porter Jr. would be ready to suit up in Week 1 against the Atlanta Falcons. That decision, McCarthy said, would be based on his health after practicing the next week. Porter Jr. didn't mention his back when pressed about when he expects to play. "Really can't speak too much about the future," Porter said. "But today I was out there today running with the guys, still trying to get back fully, but we're going to take it day by day for the most part." --Field Level Media

item.title: US and Iran exchange attacks as lull in war appears over
item.description: The U.S. and Iran found themselves back in a war footing after the most significant exchange in weeks, with Washington threatening even more devastating strikes while Iran protested an attack that it said killed five and wounded dozens of civilians at a wedding.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Ahmed Tolba
item.content:encoded: The U.S. and Iran found themselves back in a war footing on Wednesday after the most significant exchange in weeks, with Washington threatening even more devastating strikes while Iran protested an attack that it said killed five and wounded dozens of civilians at a wedding. The U.S. military's Central Command said it completed a wave of strikes against Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets on Tuesday including air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets and facilities, mine-laying capabilities, and communications sites. Iranian media reported attacks on multiple targets around the country on Tuesday, many near the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been threatening oil tankers that dare transit the narrow waterway without authorization. Iran in turn said it struck U.S. assets in Jordan and Iraq, according to official statements, while Iranian media reports said it also attacked Bahrain. Although the IRGC said it killed a large number of U.S. forces in Jordan, two U.S. officials told Reuters there had not been any casualties, according to initial assessments. Jordan's armed forces said its air defense systems dealt with 13 ballistic missiles that entered the kingdom's airspace, 10 of which were intercepted and three fell in remote areas. Bahrain said Iranian drones were intercepted and destroyed. The IRGC also said its ground forces carried out combined missile and drone attacks on U.S. bases in Erbil in northern Iraq, killing several U.S. personnel. Neither Iraq nor the U.S. had confirmed the attack. The exchange of fire marked the first serious combat since July, ending a period in which the warring parties withheld fire but also showed little interest in returning to negotiations. The lull came as the conflict appeared to be draining both sides. Iran's already ailing economy has been [USN:L8N44E0JK TEXT:"battered by war"] and its conventional military forces have been degraded. Meanwhile, with U.S. President Donald Trump confronting higher fuel prices ahead of November congressional elections, the U.S. Army has [USN:L1N43W1IH TEXT:"used up much of its global stockpile"] of highly accurate long-range missiles, Reuters reported last month, raising concerns about the military's readiness for future conflicts. Nonetheless, the renewal of hostilities produced another exchange of defiant statements. "I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing," Trump said. "They are just playing out the inevitable. When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?" Iran threatened the U.S. and its allies. "We warn that the continuation of American evil in the region will be met with heavier, more widespread, and devastating responses, and any country that cooperates with the aggressive American army must accept its dangerous consequences," Iran's joint military command said in a statement. FIVE KILLED AT WEDDING In what could be one of the more significant cases of civilian casualties in the war, five people were killed and 50 wounded at a wedding near Sirik, a coastal area on the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Red Crescent reported. The Mehr news agency said a 4-year-old child was among those killed, while the IRNA news agency, citing a provincial official, put the number of wounded at 68. U.S. officials have yet to comment on the incident. "This cruelty cannot be separated from the chain of atrocities that preceded it," Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson said in a statement, citing incidents including the blast at a school in Minab that killed 160 people at a girls' school on the first day of the war. The Pentagon has yet to issue an official finding on the Minab strike, but it may have been the result of U.S. use of [USN:L1N3ZZ12Q TEXT:"outdated targeting data"], two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters. The foreign ministry statement pledged that Iran would respond to "these savage crimes with firmness." "Those governments and international institutions that remain silent in the face of such barbarism, or seek to justify such acts, must understand that their silence is not neutrality," Iran said. "Those who remain silent today will not be immune to its consequences tomorrow."

item.title: Producción petrolera de Venezuela se duplicará en los próximos años: secretario de Energía EEUU
item.description: El secretario de Energía de Estados Unidos, Chris Wright, dijo el martes tras aterrizar en Venezuela que los acuerdos que las compañías petroleras estadounidenses y de otros países firmen el miércoles en Caracas conducirán a que la producción de crudo se duplique con creces en los próximos años.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner
item.content:encoded: El secretario de Energía de Estados Unidos, Chris Wright, dijo el martes tras aterrizar en Venezuela que los acuerdos que las compañías petroleras estadounidenses y de otros países firmen el miércoles en Caracas conducirán a que la producción de crudo se duplique con creces en los próximos años. Wright se encuentra de viaje de un día en el país miembro fundador de la OPEP, su segunda visita desde que las fuerzas estadounidenses capturaron al presidente venezolano, Nicolás Maduro, en enero. La producción petrolera venezolana, que llegó a alcanzar un máximo de más de 3 millones de barriles, se desplomó posteriormente debido a la falta de inversión, la mala gestión y las sanciones estadounidenses. En los últimos meses se ha mantenido entre 1,1 millones y 1,2 millones de barriles diarios, con un ligero aumento desde la captura de Maduro. Wright afirmó que los precios de la gasolina en Estados Unidos deberían bajar en las próximas semanas debido a las medidas que ha tomado la administración Trump para flexibilizar las regulaciones sobre las refinerías. "La inversión en estos acuerdos aumentará enormemente la producción de petróleo disponible, lo que ejercerá presión a la baja sobre los precios del crudo, pero el mayor obstáculo en este momento para los precios de la gasolina y el diésel es la capacidad de refinación", dijo Wright a los periodistas después de aterrizar.

item.title: Graham Pauley's four RBIs lift Marlins past Royals
item.description: Graham Pauley hit a two-run homer and a two-run triple, while Tyler Phillips allowed one hit over five scoreless innings, as the visiting Miami Marlins beat the Kansas City Royals 6-3 on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Graham Pauley hit a two-run homer and a two-run triple, while Tyler Phillips allowed one hit over five scoreless innings, as the visiting Miami Marlins beat the Kansas City Royals 6-3 on Tuesday night. Pauley was recalled from Triple-A Jacksonville as major league rosters were expanded and recorded a career-high four RBIs. Kyle Stowers also homered and Javier Sanoja had two hits with an RBI for the Marlins (70-69), who earned a needed win after dropping three of four at Washington. Phillips (4-6), meanwhile, allowed only a lead-off single to Carter Jensen, plus two walks, while striking out four. Jensen had two hits with an RBI and Nick Loftin clubbed a ninth-inning homer for the Royals (62-77), whose season-high seven-game home winning streak ended. Kansas City's Randy Dobnak (2-3), who entered with a 1.92 ERA in 10 appearances and eight starts, was charged with a season-high six runs, while also yielding seven hits over six-plus innings Miami, which blew a 3-0 lead against the Nationals on Monday, grabbed another early lead in this contest. In the second inning, Owen Caissie reached on an infield hit, then Pauley sent a Dobnak pitch over the fence and into the right-field bullpen. The Marlins made it 3-0 when Stowers delivered his own two-out homer, and also over the right-field fence, in the fifth. In the seventh, Pauley helped Miami break things open. After back-to-back singles from Otto Lopez and Joe Mack, both scored when Pauley lined a triple that split the right-center field gap and ended Dobnak's night. Sanoja followed with an RBI single off Anthony Gose. Kansas City finally got on the board in the eighth against Miami's Victor Vodnik. Jensen recorded an RBI double and Bobby Witt Jr. delivered a sacrifice fly to left field. The Royals initially got a third run in the frame via a Vodnik balk that scored Jensen from third, but after the umpires met to discuss, it was overturned. Kansas City manager Matt Quatraro was ejected for arguing the final decision of that call. --Field Level Media

item.title: One hiker remains missing in flood-stricken Grand Canyon
item.description: Three days after a flash flood killed two people in Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona, search teams scoured the flood zone again on Tuesday for the last confirmed missing hiker while also watching for any more victims as yet unknown to authorities.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: Three days after a flash flood killed two people in Grand Canyon National Park in Arizona, search teams scoured the flood zone again on Tuesday for the last confirmed missing hiker while also watching for any more victims as yet unknown to authorities. The National Park Service on Tuesday identified the two men whose bodies were recovered after they were swept to their deaths along the canyon floor on Saturday as John Giusti, 46, and Brent Rosenkranz, 42, both from Granbury in Texas. A third member of their hiking group, identified in news media accounts as Timothy Allen Smith, 53, remained missing, according to the Park Service. Agency officials said on Monday they held out hope that he might yet be found alive. In the immediate aftermath of the flood, authorities said that as many as 30 people were unaccounted for, before reducing the number to 15. On Tuesday, Smith was the only person conclusively still listed as missing. Justin Cully, the Grand Canyon's chief park ranger, told reporters on Monday an unspecified number of additional hikers might have been in the flood zone without officials knowing because no permits were required for daytime trail use. On Tuesday, the Park Service left open the possibility that there might be more victims. "Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with teams continuing efforts to locate the missing hiker and account for anyone else who may have been in the affected area at the time of the flood," the agency said. A total of 82 survivors were safely evacuated over the weekend, most of them by helicopter, according to Park Service incident commander Dave Black. The flood was triggered by heavy rains that sent a cascade of mud, boulders and debris rushing through Bright Angel Creek, a major side canyon that runs from the park's North Rim to the Colorado River, sweeping away trails, foot bridges and other infrastructure. The torrent also caused extensive damage to the pipeline system that supplies fresh water to the park, forcing all its overnight lodging facilities to close indefinitely, although both the South and North rims of the Grand Canyon were kept open to daytime visitors.

item.title: Lazaro Montes goes deep in debut as Mariners trounce Red Sox
item.description: Lazaro Montes homered in his major league debut for the visiting Seattle Mariners, who scored in each of the first five innings en route to a 9-6 win over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Lazaro Montes homered in his major league debut for the visiting Seattle Mariners, who scored in each of the first five innings en route to a 9-6 win over the Boston Red Sox on Tuesday night. All nine starters produced at least one hit for Seattle (65-74), which snapped a five-game skid with the 14-hit attack. Randy Arozarena contributed a three-run homer, and Dominic Canzone also went deep. Montes, a 21-year-old who was promoted from Triple-A Tacoma on Tuesday, served as Seattle's designated hitter. He was one of five Mariners with multiple hits, finishing 2-for-4 with a walk, two RBIs and two runs. The early run support was more than enough for Bryan Woo (10-9), who struck out seven in a six-inning start. Woo allowed two runs (one earned) on five hits and one walk. The Red Sox (75-64) trailed 9-1 before scoring a run in the sixth and two more in both the seventh and ninth. Mickey Gasper hit his seventh homer in his past 13 major league games. Jahmai Jones crushed a pinch-hit, two-run shot in the ninth, forcing Seattle closer Andres Munoz into the game to record the last two outs. Jedixson Paez (0-1), who was recalled from Triple-A Worcester to make his first major league start and Red Sox debut, was tagged for eight runs on 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings. He walked two and fanned three as the Red Sox took their fifth loss in seven games. Solo homers by each team's second batter made it 1-1. Canzone got Seattle started with a blast over the bullpens in right-center field before Gasper ripped a game-tying shot to virtually the same location. The Mariners used a five-run second inning to blow the game open, headlined by Arozarena's towering three-run homer down the left field line. Back-to-back hits and a walk loaded the bases before Paez recorded the first out on J.P. Crawford's sacrifice fly. Brock Rodden chopped an RBI single over first baseman Gasper to drive in a run before Arozarena went deep for the second straight night. In the third, back-to-back-to-back singles brought home a seventh Seattle run. Montes drove in Josh Naylor on a base knock through the right side. In the fourth, Julio Rodriguez and Cal Raleigh joined the hit parade with back-to-back doubles, increasing the Mariners' lead to 8-1 before Paez exited. Montes socked a solo homer to deep center leading off the fifth. Wyatt Olds, who relieved Paez, finally held Seattle scoreless in a 1-2-3 sixth. The Red Sox got back on the board in their half of the inning, as Abreu smacked a double off the left field wall and scored as Caleb Durbin reached base on an errant throw. The Red Sox drew closer on Eli White's two-run double into the left field corner in the seventh. --Field Level Media

item.title: BHP's chief commercial officer to step down in January, internal memo shows
item.description: BHP's Chief Commercial Officer Rag Udd will step down at the end of January to pursue an opportunity outside the company, according to a staff memo seen by Reuters on Tuesday, leaving open one of the miner's most difficult roles — negotiating iron ore deals with China.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Burton
item.content:encoded: BHP's Chief Commercial Officer Rag Udd will step down at the end of January to pursue an opportunity outside the company, according to a staff memo seen by Reuters on Tuesday, leaving open one of the miner's most difficult roles — negotiating iron ore deals with China. He had been seen by some analysts and investors as a contender for the top job at BHP (BHP.AX) , . That position went to Brandon Craig who started in July. Udd did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Udd, who is based in Singapore, will have worked at BHP for three decades by the time of his departure, according to the memo. He was in charge of BHP's negotiations with China Mineral Resources Group (CMRG) at a time when the state buyer ramped up pressure on BHP and other iron ore miners to win better terms for its steel makers. That pressure resulted in a number of bans on steel mills from buying its products late last year until a deal was [USN:L4N40X09W TEXT:"struck "]in April. Iron ore makers expect those negotiations to get harder, and selecting the best leader to manage that key relationship will be a top priority for Craig. Previously, Udd led BHP's Americas division from 2020 to 2024, overseeing the development of the Jansen potash project in Canada that is set to start production mid next year. He also oversaw major investments across BHP's Chilean copper operations including the Spence expansion and Escondida, the world's largest copper mine.

item.title: Susquehanna targets Hong Kong expansion to tap Chinese ETF boom, sources say
item.description: Susquehanna International Group plans to triple its office space in Hong Kong to support a major hiring push, four sources said, as the U.S. trading firm expands Asia operations and seeks deeper access to China's exchange-traded fund (ETF) market.
item.dc:creator: Summer Zhen, Clare Jim
item.content:encoded: Susquehanna International Group plans to triple its office space in Hong Kong to support a major hiring push, four sources said, as the U.S. trading firm expands Asia operations and seeks deeper access to China's exchange-traded fund (ETF) market. The Philadelphia-based group has been actively looking for new office space in the Asian financial hub over the past few weeks, said the four sources familiar with the matter but who requested anonymity as the plans are confidential. Susquehanna declined to comment. One potential option is to lease three floors covering over 50,000 square feet in Cheung Kong Center II, a newly redeveloped office tower in Central, three of the sources said, adding that a relocation plan has yet to be confirmed. The global systematic market maker and trading firm currently occupies less than 20,000 square feet in the AIA Central commercial building in the city's main business district. The office space expansion will back Susquehanna's ambitious hiring plans in the city, two of the sources said. A separate fifth source with knowledge of the matter said that the firm is focusing on opportunities in China's rapidly growing market for ETFs and other assets to better support its global business. Susquehanna will become the latest among global trading companies to [USN:L1N3SK03D TEXT:"accelerate"] growth in major Asian markets and [USN:L3N3QB0PQ TEXT:"leverage"] Hong Kong as a gateway to trade in Chinese markets. Its peers Jane Street and IMC Group [USN:L6N40I0K8 TEXT:"snapped up"] Hong Kong office space over the past year or so, boosting recovery prospects for the city's top-tier office property market after nearly seven straight years of decline. HONG KONG JOB POSTINGS Susquehanna has posted over 20 Hong Kong-based full-time and internship positions just over the past week, spanning roles from quant developer, engineer and research, to compliance and talent sourcer, as per LinkedIn and job portal eFinancialCareers. With its Asia headquarters in Sydney, Susquehanna currently employs about 70 people in Hong Kong, its website showed. Its other regional offices are in mainland China, Mumbai, Singapore and Tokyo. As one of the earliest and top investors in China's biggest unicorn ByteDance, Susquehanna's global businesses span quant trading and institutional sales, to private equity and prediction markets. Susquehanna's Hong Kong expansion plan also comes as China has been [USN:L3N3QP06T TEXT:"looking at"] allowing Western trading firms to act as market makers in its rapidly growing ETF market, Reuters reported last year, citing sources. Shanghai Stock Exchange data shows China emerged as Asia's biggest ETF market last year with assets exceeding 6 trillion yuan ($892.5 billion). The number of onshore-listed ETF products was 1,381 last year, up 36% from 2024. In the past few years, China has allowed various types of ETFs to be traded, including thematic and fixed-income ones, allowing global market makers to access a wider array of investment instruments, one of the sources said. ETF market makers serve as liquidity providers, offering continuous bid and ask quotes for ETF shares. This allows investors to trade products efficiently and at a lower cost, while market makers profit from the spread. ($1 = 6.7228 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: Indian shares open lower as widening Iran conflict sends oil higher
item.description: Indian shares opened lower on Wednesday, in line with global markets, as oil prices surged to a near-six-week high after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, intensifying the Middle East conflict and renewing concerns over inflation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian shares opened lower on Wednesday, in line with global markets, as oil prices surged to a near-six-week high after the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes overnight, intensifying the Middle East conflict and renewing concerns over inflation. The Nifty 50 (.NSEI) fell 0.82% to 23,858 and the BSE Sensex (.BSESN) shed 0.61% to 76,471.32 as of 9:15 a.m. IST. All 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) lost 0.4% and 0.5%, respectively. Brent crude rose 1% to $95.4 a barrel, paring some gains after hitting a near-six-week-high earlier in the session, triggering a drop in Asian markets and lifting global bond yields on worries of a near-term U.S. rate hike. Higher U.S. rates make emerging markets less attractive for global investors. The U.S. [USN:L8N44T0TP TEXT:"said"] it had launched a series of airstrikes against targets in Iran overnight, prompting an Iranian response in a renewed escalation of tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Teenager Frodin hopes to meet idol Serena after US Open debut
item.description: Thea Frodin made her U.S. Open debut on Tuesday but one dream remains unfulfilled for the 17-year-old, who is still waiting to meet Serena Williams five years after appearing as the American's tennis double in the film "King Richard".
item.dc:creator: Janina Rios
item.content:encoded: Thea Frodin made her U.S. Open debut on Tuesday but one dream remains unfulfilled for the 17-year-old, who is still waiting to meet Serena Williams five years [USN:L1N44R069 TEXT:"after appearing"] as the American's tennis double in the film "King Richard". Serena, a 23-times Grand Slam champion, returned to the court for the first time in nearly four years at the Queen's Club Championships in London in June and is back at Flushing Meadows competing in doubles with sister Venus. "Hopefully I can get the chance soon to get the opportunity to meet her," Frodin told reporters after losing 6-1 6-1 to world number two Elena Rybakina on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Frodin earned a wildcard for the U.S. Open by winning the USTA Girls' 18s National Championships, and while her Grand Slam debut against Rybakina was a harsh introduction to life at the elite level, she said it was a valuable lesson for her career. "It was a fun experience to kind of see how the best players in the world, how they hit their balls and their shots," she said. "My goal on court is always to have an aggressive game style. Today I feel like it was a bit harder to bring that out. Hopefully the next time I can be more experienced and see what I can do." Frodin said she had managed to handle the attention surrounding her unusual connection to Serena, though acknowledged it was difficult to escape the headlines before her debut. "I think it's hard to get away from all of that. It's kind of just about accepting it and not letting it get to you," she added. Actor Will Smith, who won an Academy Award for playing Serena's father Richard Williams in the film, reposted one of Frodin's social media posts before her match, something she described as "pretty cool". Frodin plans to play the girls' U.S. Open next week and finish high school before deciding whether to turn professional or play college tennis. "I'm not rushing into kind of making a decision with all that," she said. "I'm taking this year and next year to finish high school and then see where I am then."

item.title: Gold hits over 3-week low as MidEast tensions fan rate-hike fears
item.description: Gold fell on Wednesday to its lowest in more than three weeks, as the escalating Middle East conflict lifted oil prices and stoked inflation and rate-hike fears, while investors focused on upcoming U.S. jobs data.
item.dc:creator: Ashitha Shivaprasad
item.content:encoded: Gold fell on Wednesday to its lowest in more than three weeks, as the escalating Middle East conflict lifted oil prices and stoked inflation and rate-hike fears, while investors focused on upcoming U.S. jobs data. Spot gold was down 0.6% at $4,304.01 per ounce by 0017 GMT, its lowest since August 7. Prices were headed for a fourth straight session of losses and remained below the 200-day moving average, a closely watched technical level. U.S. gold futures for December delivery fell 1% to $4,350.80. The U.S. dollar held firm, making greenback-priced metals costlier for buyers using other currencies. The U.S. launched a barrage of [USN:L8N44T0TP TEXT:"airstrikes"] against Iran on Tuesday, prompting Iranian retaliation, in the most serious escalation in weeks. Oil prices rose for a third straight session, while U.S. Treasury yields advanced. "A rebound in oil prices after renewed U.S.-Iran tensions added to inflation concerns. A pricier crude could continue to tighten monetary policy expectations and drive yields higher, limiting any rebound potential for gold," said Bas Kooijman, CEO and asset manager of DHF Capital S.A. Although gold is seen as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates weigh on its appeal as it offers no yield. Traders are pricing in a 67% chance of a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's policy meeting this month, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. Fed Governor [USN:S0N4490C0 TEXT:"Michael Barr"] said if inflation does not cool quickly, it will be time for the central bank to raise rates. Last week, Fed Chairman [USN:L6N44P0MM TEXT:"Kevin Warsh"] nodded to the prospect of a rate hike. The ADP employment report is due later in the day and the more crucial nonfarm payrolls data is due on Friday. "Softer figures could ease the pressure on gold, while stronger data or more hawkish Fed comments may extend the decline," Kooijman said. Among other metals, spot silver lost 1% to $63.60 per ounce, platinum edged 1% lower to $1,722.23 and palladium fell 1.4% to $1,292.21.

item.title: Takaichi’s Japan risks ceding policy control to US
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's suggestion that the BOJ will raise rates in September has already led markets to price it in, undermining Japan's monetary independence. It shows US support for the yen carries conditions that could derail the prime minister's fiscal splurge.
item.dc:creator: Hudson Lockett
item.content:encoded: Where is Japanese monetary policy set? As far as traders are concerned, the answer is increasingly Washington. On Tuesday, yields on 10-year Japanese government bonds surpassed 3% for the first time in three decades, after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Japan’s central bank governor and finance minister to raise interest rates on the sidelines of this week’s G20 summit, per broadcaster NHK. The longer Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi acquiesces to such pressure tactics, the less faith markets will have in her country’s capacity to chart its own financial course. On the heels of Monday’s report, Bessent took [USN:SPN44S00O TEXT:"another striking step"] in telling CNBC that “I have information that the market doesn’t have, and it’s my belief that the Japanese government and the [Bank of Japan] will do the things that will lead to a stronger yen.” The bank’s ultimate decision and what Bessent really knows are both beside the point: the comments lock in market expectations that the central bank will raise rates on September 18 and amount to interference in a close ally’s monetary policymaking. That’s in contrast to July’s joint intervention, where Washington acted as junior partner by selling down its stash of euros to support the yen. Takaichi hasn't yet spoken out against U.S. encroachment on the independence of central bank Governor Kazuo Ueda. This is probably because Bessent’s stated preference for a strong yen helps stave off greater currency weakness and keep afloat her ambitions for a 370 trillion yen ($2.3 trillion) investment splurge, despite investor concerns attendant bond issuance will again weaken the yen. Of course, Japanese officials could choose to go at it alone and swallow the inflationary costs of currency depreciation. On Monday finance minister Satsuki Katayama played down Bessent’s call for higher rates. Regardless, Japan's bond market closely tracking his statements reflects Tokyo surrendering some of its policy autonomy. That's a real problem because the Trump administration's aims won't always align with those of governments whose currencies it's propping up. One reason Bessent may have bought the yen, for example, is that Japan mounting a defence on its own would likely entail selling down its massive trove of U.S. bonds. But he presumably doesn't want to keep dipping into America's finite foreign-exchange pot either, especially since the yen has already walked back half its joint-intervention gains. That might explain why, in an [USN:L4N44R06P TEXT:"interview with Reuters"] on Monday, Bessent described “Takaichinomics” chiefly as a shareholder-friendly deregulatory drive, while suggesting Japan "should just sit back and enjoy the success of Abenomics". It's a not-so-subtle attempt to overwrite Takaichi's [USN:L6N43X09H TEXT:"signature spendthrift agenda"]. Tokyo may soon discover that borrowed support comes with borrowed priorities. Follow Hudson Lockett on Bluesky and X . Yields on Japanese 10-year government bonds rose above 3% on September 1 for the first time since 1996. The move came after broadcaster NHK reported that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on August 31 had told Japan’s finance minister and central bank governor in separate meetings that their country should raise interest rates. Bessent said later that day in an interview with CNBC: “I have information that the market doesn’t have, and it’s my belief that the Japanese government and the BOJ will do the things that will lead to a stronger yen.” Bloomberg reported on August 25 that Tokyo will seek a record 36.6 trillion yen just for debt-servicing costs in the next fiscal year.
